Documents and sections

Source: R/doc.R
pub_doc.Rd

pub_doc() creates a document and pub_section() is used to create sections within a document. Documents are usually created as part of a pipeflow pipeline: first, the parts of the document (tables, figures, text) are created in separate steps, and then a layout step arranges them into sections (see Examples).

Usage

pub_doc(..., title = NULL, subtitle = NULL, meta = list())

pub_section(
  title,
  ...,
  numbered = TRUE,
  landscape = FALSE,
  page_break = NULL,
  on_empty = c("drop", "keep", "stop")
)

Arguments

...

Children: sections and outputs (see "Children" in Details).

title

character(1) title of the document or section.

subtitle

character(1) subtitle of the document or NULL.

meta

Named list of document metadata (see "Metadata" in Details).

numbered

TRUE: the section is numbered (children of unnumbered sections are unnumbered).

landscape

TRUE: the section is placed on landscape pages (DOCX, PDF).

page_break

NULL: level-1 sections start on a new page in paged formats; TRUE/FALSE override this.

on_empty

when an empty section is placed into a document or section, it is dropped ("drop", default), kept ("keep") or an error is signalled ("stop").

Value

A pub_doc or pub_section object.

Details

Children

The children (...) are interpreted as follows:

ChildBecomes
sectiona section
listone sub-section per named element (see below)
data.frame, matrixa table with default settings (see pub_table())
huxtablea table
character vectorMarkdown text (see pub_text())
ggplot, grDevices::recordPlot(), pub_figure()a figure
htmlwidgetan interactive widget
pub_raw()your own code, inserted as-is
pub_pagebreak()a page break (DOCX, PDF)
pub_toc()a table of contents
failed step, error item of pub_out()an error box
NULL, empty textnothing
pipelinean error (place the outputs of its steps instead)

Names of list elements become the titles of their sub-sections while unnamed elements are placed directly (no sub-section). To define the caption, digits and other settings of a table, use pub_table(). Any other classes are converted with as_pub_output() (see pub_type()).

Metadata

Metadata of a document:

KeyMeaning
title, subtitletitle lines (also arguments)
authoruser name, e.g. for the trace stamp
timetime of the document (POSIXct)
app, versionname and version of the application
header, footernamed character, keys left, center, right

A blank string ("" or only whitespace) as title, subtitle, author, app or version counts as not given. You can add keys of your own: pubflow keeps them but doesn't check or use them.

Failed steps

A failed step does not have to stop the document: write the inputs of a layout step as ~try(step) and run the pipeline with pipeflow::pip_run(x, on_error = "continue"). The document can then still be rendered and shows an error box with the step's error message where the step's output would be (also for steps that did not run). In contrast, with a plain ~step the layout step is skipped if the step fails, so there is no document. With the default pipeflow::pip_run(x, on_error = "stop") the run stops immediately at the first failure.

Saving documents

A document holds only the outputs, not the pipeline, so it can be saved with saveRDS() and rendered later or in another R session. One pitfall: a ggplot remembers where it was made. If a plot step is written as a lambda inside the function that builds the pipeline (\(data = ~data) ggplot(...)), the saved document includes the whole pipeline. To avoid this, define plot functions outside the function that builds the pipeline. Plots that a step renders itself (pub_figure(render = TRUE)) have no such problem.

See also

pub_type(), pub_table(), pub_text(), pub_figure()

Examples

p <- pipeflow::pip_new("demo") |>
    # Steps that make the content
    pipeflow::pip_add("data", \(n = 4) {
        data.frame(x = seq_len(n), y = seq_len(n)^2)
    }) |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("table", \(data = ~data) {
        pub_table(data, caption = "Data")
    }) |>
    pipeflow::pip_add("mean", \(data = ~data) {
        pub_format_num(mean(data$y), "Mean: %.2f")
    }) |>
    # The layout step arranges their outputs into a document
    pipeflow::pip_add("report", \(table = ~table, mean = ~mean) {
        pub_doc(
            pub_section("Data", table),
            pub_section("Results", mean),
            title = "Demo"
        )
    })

# Run the pipeline and take the document from the layout step
pipeflow::pip_run(p, lgr = NULL)
doc <- p[["report", "out"]]
doc
#> <pubflow document> "Demo"
#> # Data
#>   table "Data"
#> # Results
#>   text "Mean: 7.50"

# A document can also be made directly, without a pipeline
pub_doc(
    pub_section(
        "Introduction",
        pub_text("The study has **three** batches."),
        data.frame(batch = c("A", "B", "C"), n = c(4L, 4L, 4L))
    ),
    pub_section("Annex", pub_session_info(), numbered = FALSE),
    title = "Analysis report",
    meta = list(author = "Jane Doe", app = "demo", version = "1.0")
)
#> <pubflow document> "Analysis report"
#> # Introduction
#>   text "The study has **three** batches."
#>   table
#> # Annex [unnumbered]
#>   ## Session info
#>     text "```"
